extracted.intended_audience: registered CTE apprenticeship program sponsors, Registration Agencies, State CTE Agencies, employers, industry stakeholders, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the proposed regulatory requirements and quality standards for Registered CTE (Career and Technical Education) apprenticeship programs, including required content and validation of industry skills frameworks, minimum hours for instruction and on-the-job training, assessment, wages, ratios, credentialing, and transparency/feedback processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry skills framework content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(b)(1)(i): an industry skills framework must include a structure for the development of professional behaviors, workplace competencies, and academic competencies required by an industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of professional behaviors include reliability, initiative, interpersonal skills, and adaptability; academic competencies might include effective reading and writing, problem-solving, and critical thinking; workplace competencies might include collaboration and teamwork, oral and written communication, and customer service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry skills framework validation and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(b)(1)(ii): industry skills frameworks must be validated, widely recognized, and nationally applicable in the industry to which the framework is intended to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should recognize cross-cutting skills across industries and align, to the extent possible, with CTE Career Clusters. The Department seeks comment on interconnections and alignment with State and local advisory council processes to strengthen framework development and use in registered CTE apprenticeship standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry skills framework development stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department envisions leveraging the National Occupational Standards for Apprenticeship process (§ 29.13) and anticipates that initial development will engage a broad set of industry stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry stakeholders, State CTE Agencies, educational and workforce development experts, and other leaders are expected to be instrumental in developing frameworks. State CTE standards may provide foundations for some frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum on-the-job training hours (900 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(b)(1)(iii) & § 29.24(c): skills and competencies specified in the on-the-job training outline must be obtained through attainment of at least 900 hours of on-the-job training over the course of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 900 hours may be spread across multiple years. Department rationale is to ensure sufficient paid employment time for industrywide/industry-sector technical competencies; based on State youth apprenticeship models (e.g., 450 hours/year). The Department solicits comment on whether 900 hours is appropriate or should be adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of skills framework with approved CTE program
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(b)(1)(iv): an industry skills framework must align with an approved CTE program so the employment component provides appropriate practical on-the-job training supported by CTE apprenticeship-related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment is intended with National Career Clusters® Framework and associated CTE programs to create systematic cohesion and seamless transitions for CTE apprentices to participate, progress, and complete a registered CTE apprenticeship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-validated ongoing evaluation methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(b)(1)(v): industry skills frameworks must detail industry-validated methods for ongoing evaluations to assess an apprentice's attainment of a competency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular evaluations are a central program design element that verify programs are preparing apprentices for careers. Designs of assessments are left to program sponsors, with industry and education experts instrumental in framework development. Registered CTE apprenticeship evaluations should be different in form from the more robust end-point assessments proposed for registered apprenticeship under subpart A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for regular evaluations (assessment frequency/design)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department proposes including regular evaluations as a required element of registered CTE apprenticeship programs to ensure apprentices are regularly evaluated as they progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While regular evaluations are required, the Department does not expect registered CTE apprenticeship to require occupational proficiency for all participants; evaluations may be tailored to foundational industry skills. The Department seeks comment on whether an industry-recognized end-point assessment should be required to strengthen labor-market relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator solicitation of public feedback and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(b)(2): the Administrator must solicit public feedback (including industry) when evaluating the suitability of industry skills frameworks and provide at least 30 days of public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OA would maintain a publicly accessible link to approved and not-approved frameworks. The process should continuously update frameworks to reflect changing industry needs and ensure applicability and high quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of industry data to validate frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(b)(2): the Administrator may use relevant industry data or information to validate the relevance of industry skills frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant resources may include O*NET, BLS industry and occupational data, and other federal or industry sources to ensure frameworks align with industry needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum standards of registered CTE apprenticeship (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c): all registered CTE apprenticeship programs must include minimum standards to ensure consistent high-quality education and training, safety, accessibility, and protection from exploitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards will largely follow subpart A labor standards (progressive wages, ratios, safety, advanced standing, cost transparency, protections), but differ by incorporating industry skills frameworks, State-approved CTE instruction, minimum credit requirements, and linkages to postsecondary programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-job training outline alignment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c)(1): program sponsors must include an on-the-job training (OJT) outline that aligns with an approved industry skills framework in program standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry skills frameworks guide determination of work activities leading to proficiency. OJT outlines should provide measurable proficiency in industry-recognized skills and competencies. Registration Agencies have discretion to decide whether a sponsor's OJT outline aligns with an approved framework; sponsors should balance customization with industry validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CTE apprenticeship-related instruction minimum hours (540 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c)(2): program sponsors must include a description of CTE apprenticeship-related instruction that at minimum includes a State-approved CTE program and has a duration of at least 540 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 540 hours is intended to allow completion of foundational and advanced coursework needed for postsecondary success and credential attainment. The Department allows flexibility for sponsors to determine additional hours based on State/local programs and career pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum 12 postsecondary credit hours requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c)(2): CTE apprentices must receive a minimum of 12 postsecondary credit hours as part of their program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'credit hour' aligns with the Higher Education Act definition; generally each credit hour ≈30 clock hours, so 12 credits ≈360 clock hours. Postsecondary credit hours may be acquired as part of OJT when combined with instruction to total at least 12 credits. Purpose is to support progress toward recognized postsecondary credentials and to capture benefits of dual enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in how CTE instruction hours and credits are attained
rubrics_metrics.description: The remaining CTE apprenticeship-related instruction hours beyond the 12-credit portion may be acquired through additional postsecondary credit hours, secondary education, or other industry/employer-designed related instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 540 hour floor allows flexibility in how sponsors define and apply hours; sponsors may offer instruction while students are in high school, postsecondary education, or spanning both. The Department solicits comments on whether 540 hours is the right floor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of recognized postsecondary credentials and awarding entity
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c)(3): program sponsors must include a description of any recognized postsecondary credentials awarded during or at completion of the program, including any associate/baccalaureate degree and the amount of postsecondary credit hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors must include the name of the credential- or certificate-awarding entity (typically an accredited institution). This disclosure helps Registration Agencies build high-quality programs and evaluate credentialing outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program outcome description requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c)(4): sponsors must describe how the program will result in (a) selection into a subpart A registered apprenticeship, (b) enrollment in a postsecondary program, (c) employment, or (d) some combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Achieving any one of these outcomes is considered a key success metric. Programs should establish documented relationships with subpart A apprenticeships and institutions of higher education, especially where such partnerships exist in the sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of employment in OJT and criteria in OJT outline
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c)(5): sponsors must include a description of the employment in which CTE apprentices will be employed for OJT with criteria included in the OJT outline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because industry skills frameworks may be broader than single-occupation training, this requirement helps Registration Agencies determine that employment is relevant to the skills framework and that apprentices will achieve the identified skills on the job.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage schedule and minimum wage floor requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c)(6): written standards must include wages that CTE apprentices will receive, including a progressively increasing schedule; entry wage may not be less than the Fair Labor Standards Act minimum wage unless higher law applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The graduated wage schedule should increase over the apprenticeship term to reflect progressive acquisition of skills and competencies. The Department encourages employers, where possible, to provide wages or fringe benefits during CTE apprenticeship-related instruction, though sponsors may be less likely to provide wages for instruction hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in wages and employee classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Wages paid must not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age (40+), genetic information, or disability, consistent with 29 CFR part 30; CTE apprentices who meet the definition of employee must not be misclassified as independent contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors and participating employers must comply with applicable nondiscrimination law and ensure proper worker classification under the Internal Revenue Code and FLSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprentice-to-journeyworker ratio requirement (safety-centered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed § 29.24(c)(7): sponsor's apprentice-to-journeyworker ratio must be approved by a Registration Agency and be centered on proper safety, health, supervision, and training of the CTE apprentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider factors such as exposure to hazardous conditions and risk of serious bodily injury or death when establishing numeric ratios. While a 1:1 ratio has been common in subpart A, registered CTE apprenticeship may require greater scrutiny for youth apprentices; ratios must be consistent with collective bargaining agreements and applicable laws and clearly described in context (workforce, workplace, job site, department, or plant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design expectation — not requiring occupational proficiency baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department does not view attainment of occupational proficiency as an appropriate baseline requirement for registered CTE apprenticeship programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered CTE apprenticeship focuses more on foundational industry skills and may serve more secondary and postsecondary student apprentices by introducing career options, developing professional behaviors, and conferring occupational competencies that aid employment and further education; some programs may blend CTE frameworks with occupational work process schedules for mastery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration dependency on approved industry skills frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: A potential program sponsor must have an industry skills framework developed and approved by the Administrator before properly developing and aligning their OJT outlines with the required framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation will require time for subregulatory guidance, written coordination agreements between Registration Agencies and State CTE Agencies, and a robust development process engaging Perkins and National Apprenticeship System stakeholders; until frameworks are approved sponsors cannot fully align OJT outlines.
